title: Oliver fires Jimmy Palao and the union fines him $200
summary: Oliver let Jimmy Palao go in San Francisco without notice, Local 6 fined him, and the Plantation date in Chicago was stopped until the fines were paid.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: How we come to get Baby Joe Fired Jimmy Psido David Dodds, was in San Francisco (Unintelligible).

He played violin. Also clarinet. And Joe let him go. So this boy Minor Hall, we called him Ram, said, 'Well, why are you going to fire this man? We're at the end of the Southern Pacific Line and (Unintelligible). He said, 'I've got a lot to do with it. I don't think it's right.' Then he said, 'Well, if that's the case, I'll go too.'

That was the drummer, (Unintelligible). So finally, he went to the union and told them about it -- number six -- and said, "Did you get a notice?" And he said, "No." "Did you give him a notice?" He said, "No." And they said, "Well, he done sent for another drummer trombonist." He said, "What?" He sent for Baby Davey Dodds. He's in St. Louis. Baby Davey Dodd's coming in from St. Louis and (Unintelligible). So they called in Joe and Joe -- told Joe he had to pay Jimmy -- give Jimmy two weeks, pay Jimmy for two weeks. And Ram had to get two weeks pay, but he had to give a notice. See?

MR. GARLAND: And fined Joe $200.00. Joe left for Frisco and went on back to Chicago, and he thought he was going to get by, you know. He went to open up the PLANTATION on 31st Street, near Cottage Grove. That night, everybody setting up (Unintelligible). Big band, too. 12 pieces. Joe's sitting up there getting ready to play and the business agent walked in and said, "I'm sorry. Don't nobody move." "Your band can't play here." Told the lady "This band can't play." The place is like that, you know? (Unintelligible). Joe said, "Why can't I play?" Said, "You owe $200.00 to number six. You runned off and didn't pay. So now each one of these men here has got to pay $100.00." That was $1,200.00 right there.

That's $1,400.00. So he said, 'I'm sorry lady, if you want to make it good, you can't do that to me.' (Unintelligible). Give us a check or do something about it. Some way or another, she did, Miss Barnett. She said, 'Well, I'll stand responsible for the money.' They had to pay. That ain't no joke, that's really the facts.
